clue.text: After review of command, man broadcasting is happy

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the word for command is read backwards

parts.note: a law is a command laid down by authority
a king is a piece, or man, in chess
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A man delighted after looking over an order while on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' reverses only the command word; 'man' is a chess piece, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone walking on air is elated, floating with joy.

clue.text: Opposing sides on island in aftermath becoming hostile

indicators.note: the pieces for sides and island sit inside the word for aftermath

parts.note: in the wake of something means in its aftermath
right and left, R and L, are opposite sides

explanation.surface: Factions on an island turn aggressive after some disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposing sides' are right and left, a common crossword pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: warlike behaviour is aggressive and inclined to fight.

clue.text: Antagonist facetiously called judge 500 things, but not Ms

parts.note: m'lud is the jokey rendering of my lord, the way a judge is addressed in court
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: the clue explicitly says the things are wanted without the two letters M and S

parts.note: items are things
the letters M and S taken literally

explanation.surface: Someone sardonically names a judge and lists five hundred items, omitting any titles for women.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M and S from ITEMS leaves ITE. The definition is fair because Luddites famously opposed new machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luddite is an opponent of new technology, so an antagonist of progress.

clue.text: Nice lad struggling with it getting no different

indicators.note: a struggling lad is in disarray, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A pleasant boy battling with some task gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike show no difference between them.

clue.text: Prepares good flyers, apart from heading

indicators.note: the word for flyers loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: birds are flyers

explanation.surface: Someone readies decent pilots, except the one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRDS without its head is IRDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird oneself is to get ready for action, as in girding one's loins.

clue.text: Understood beef said to be fresh cut

indicators.note: said signals that the two words for understood and beef are spoken and heard

parts.note: understood means knew, and to beef is to moan or complain

explanation.surface: A butcher's description of meat that was just sliced, which the customer grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW MOAN, spoken, matches the hyphenated answer; the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that is new-mown has just been cut, so it is freshly trimmed.

clue.text: Regularly ignored disdain of jerk being foolish

indicators.note: every other letter of the words disdain and of is skipped, keeping the even ones

parts.note: a tic is a sudden involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Someone keeps brushing off a fool's contempt, which seems silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping alternate letters of 'disdain of' keeps IDIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: idiotic behaviour is stupid and senseless.

clue.text: Animals here perhaps go quietly with shyness

parts.note: game as in up for it matches go in all systems go, willing
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
reserve is shyness or restraint

explanation.surface: Advice to proceed softly and timidly.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME means willing, as does go when someone is all go. 'Perhaps' signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract of land kept for wild creatures to be hunted, so beasts are found there.

clue.text: Reduce a part of the nose

parts.note: the bridge is the bony upper part of the nose

explanation.surface: Advice for shrinking a feature of one's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or cut it down.

clue.text: Getting involved in disputes, stop troublemakers

indicators.note: the word for stop gets inside the word for disputes

parts.note: rows are quarrels or disputes
an engine that dies stops

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop meddling in arguments, aimed at hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' reads as a command but is just a synonym for die, as an engine stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdies are noisy, disorderly people who stir up trouble.

clue.text: Yielding resistance in uncontrollable dinner urges

indicators.note: the letter for resistance sits within the rearranged letters
urges that cannot be controlled run wild, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Giving in to irresistible cravings for an evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of DINNER URGES takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: surrendering means giving way or submitting.

clue.text: Snobby model wearing hat back to front

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is read in reverse order
the word for model goes inside the word for hat, as if it had the hat on

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat
to sit is to pose as a model

explanation.surface: A haughty model wears her headgear the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' reverses the whole assembly, not just the hat. Tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours a select few, which makes that person snobbish.

clue.text: Something like an owl on son's arm

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
an owl hoots, so it is a hooter

explanation.surface: An owl perched on the arm of a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon here, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter is slang for a gun, and a gun is a firearm.

clue.text: Bailiff's about late in the day

parts.note: re means about or concerning
eve is the evening, the end of the day

explanation.surface: A bailiff arrives in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a medieval English officer overseeing a manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official much like a steward or bailiff.

clue.text: Revised role, cinch to record

indicators.note: a revised text is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's rewritten part is easy to put on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To chronicle events is to set them down in a historical account.

clue.text: Preparing beetroot before serving

indicators.note: the colour word comes first, ahead of the word for serving

parts.note: beetroot red, a deep red colour
acting as something is serving as it

explanation.surface: Getting beetroot ready before it is dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' looks culinary but means acting, as in serving as chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Redacting is editing or preparing a text for publication.

clue.text: Partially rigid house's one with worn-out exterior

parts.note: a semi, short for semi-detached, is a house; with the apostrophe S

indicators.note: the word for worn-out forms the outside, around the letter for one

parts.note: old things are worn out
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A house that is part solid has a shabby outside.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house; I goes inside OLD to give OLID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something semisolid is half firm, between liquid and solid.

clue.text: Standardised drum rearranged with most of load

indicators.note: these letters are put in a fresh order
the word load loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Rearranging a drum alongside most of a cargo, for uniformity.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAD loses D to give LOA, then DRUM plus LOA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Modular construction uses standard interchangeable units.

clue.text: Searched and searched, getting primarily rushed for time

indicators.note: the word getting the replacement swaps one letter for another, with for signalling the swap

parts.note: scouted means searched or explored

indicators.note: the first letter of rushed is taken

explanation.surface: Someone hunted and hunted in a hurry against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In SCOUTED, T (time) is replaced by R, the first letter of 'rushed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to search thoroughly, so a scoured area has been combed.

clue.text: Prompt to receive posh noble

indicators.note: the word for prompt takes in the letter for posh

parts.note: to prod is to prompt or urge
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A nudge to welcome a high-class aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble bearing is a proud, dignified one.

clue.text: Ancient city's millions held by second religious leader?

indicators.note: the letter for millions is held within the word for religious leader

parts.note: the Pope leads the Catholic Church
II is the regnal number for the second, as in a pope's title

explanation.surface: A city's wealth seized by a later pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the regnal numeral following a papal name, as in John Paul II.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Old kit is full of new germs

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or kit

indicators.note: the word is gets filled with the letter for new

explanation.surface: An old outfit crawling with fresh bacteria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'germs' looks like bacteria but means beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The germ of an idea is its starting point or source.

clue.text: Do read mobile containing one sent message

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the numeral for one
mobile means moving freely, so the letters shift

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An instruction to read a text on a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of DO READ takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio is to transmit a communication by wireless.

clue.text: Nerd heads for dictionary with competition coming up

indicators.note: the leading letters of the words dictionary and with are taken
in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee

explanation.surface: A swot makes for the dictionary as a spelling contest approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE read upwards gives EEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a dull, studious, socially awkward person.

clue.text: Less awkward if back girdled in advance, before run

indicators.note: the assembled piece comes ahead of the letter for run
the reversed letters are surrounded by the word for advance

parts.note: to come is to approach or advance

indicators.note: the word if is read backwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Would it be easier if one's corset were fitted early, before a jog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'girdled' suggests a corset, but it just means surrounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfier means more comfortable, so less uneasy.

clue.text: Add to rum order of general

indicators.note: rum means odd, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An officer commands that rum be added to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to add to its size.

clue.text: I head around Rhode Island from peninsula

indicators.note: the slang word for head goes around the state abbreviation

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Someone sets off from Rhode Island toward a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is slang bean, not the I that leads the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian refers to the peninsula of Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Small hero nervous of big dragons

indicators.note: nervous letters are jittery, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little champion is scared of huge dragons.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobbit of The Lord of the Rings is a diminutive protagonist.
